newsitem.title: Afghanistan: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, MARCH 3-SUNDAY, MARCH 9 (PAGE 1/3 - MONDAY).
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, MARCH 3-SUNDAY, MARCH 9 (PAGE 1/3 - MONDAY).

text.p: **** HIGHLIGHTS **** BRUSSELS - EU environment ministers meet (Sunday-Tuesday); discussions focus on climate change and the Auto Oil programme. MOSCOW - EU and Russia hold summit (Monday); Commission President Santer, Commissioner van den Broek, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo attend; main discussions focus on EU-Russia partnership and cooperation agreement; World Trade Organisation; drugs and crime; EU enlargement; investment. BRUSSELS - Inter-governmental conference representatives meet (Monday-Tuesday). FRANKFURT - European Commissioner de Silguy attends European Monetary Institute meeting (Tuesday). BRUSSELS - European People's Party holds extraordinary summit (Tuesday); government heads, European Commission President Santer and EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles attend; discussions focus on the state of the inter-governmental conference and EU enlargement - followed by a closing news conference. BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday). BRUSSELS - Belgian King Albert meets European Commission President Santer (Wednesday). BRUSSELS - EU telecoms ministers meet (Thursday); discussions focus on rules to cover voice telephony in a competitive environment. BRUSSELS - European Commissioner Flynn holds news conference on equal rights between men and women for International Women's Day (Thursday). BRUSSELS - European Commissioner Bangemann attends EP and Council Conciliation Committee meeting to discuss decision on guidelines for trans-European telecoms networks (Friday). MONDAY, MARCH 3 BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Environment Council (1000/0900 GMT) (and Tuesday). Agenda includes: - Council conclusions on Community strategy on climate change. - Orientation debate on Commission communication on implementing Community environmental law. - International accord on humane trapping standards between the European Community, Canada and Russia - State of work on negotiations with third countries. - Proposal for a Council decision on a Community action programme promoting non-governmental organisations primarily active in the field of environmental protection. - Future strategy for the control of atmospheric emissions from road transport taking into account the results of the auto-oil programme. a) Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels and amending Council directive 93/12/EEC; b) Proposal for an EP and Council directive on measures to be taken against air pollution by emissions from motor vehicles and amending Council directives 70/156/EEC and 70/220/EEC. c) Orientation debate on second auto-oil programme. - Proposal for Council directive reducing composed organic emissions due to the use of organic solvents in certain industrial activities. - Commission presentation on the proposal for a framework directive on water. - Orientation debate on the Commission's communication to the Council and EP on environmental accords. - (1630/1530 GMT) Joint meeting with Central and Eastern European Countries: - State of work on the follow-up to the last joint ministerial meeting particularly on the approximation of environmental legislation. - Climate change and environment policy: a challenge for energy conservation. BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0900 GMT). BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Inter-governmental conference (IGC) representatives meet (and Tuesday). BRUSSELS - EP Socialists hold conference on "Women's rights" (1000/0900 GMT). Main discussions focus on equal access to money and power; the inter-governmental conference on EU reform; violence against women. Women from Afghanistan, Algeria and Africa attend. Speakers include: European Commissioner Gradin. Venue: EP, Espace Leopold Building. ROME (NEW ITEM) - European People's Party hosts celebration to mark 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome; EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles attends. BRUSSELS - Scotland Europa hosts launch of "European regions' education network (EREN)" (0930/0830 GMT) (and Tuesday). Venue: Espace Messelle, 40 rue des Drapiers. Contact: Scotland Europa (322) 502 5028. BRUSSELS - The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) holds conference on the environmental, technological and economic aspects of copper recycling (and Tuesday). MOSCOW (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU and Russia hold summit; Commission President Santer, Commissioner van den Broek, Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo attend. Main discussions focus on EU-Russia partnership and cooperation agreement; World Trade Organisation; drugs and crime; enlargement; investment. News conference at 1500/1200 GMT at the European Commission representation. Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (Tuesday-Wednesday) TUESDAY, MARCH 4 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Environment Council continues (second of two days). BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Inter-governmental conference representatives continue meeting (second of two days). (Possibly) closing news conference. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer, Commissioners Fischler and Bonino meet Irish Prime Minister John Bruton. FRANKFURT (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner de Silguy attends European Monetary Institute meeting. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European People's Party (EPP) holds extraordinary summit (1400/1300 GMT). Attendees include: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, European Commission President Santer and EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles. Discussions focus on the state of the inter-governmental conference (IGC) and EU enlargement. EPP President Wilfried Martens holds news conference at 1800/1700 GMT. Venue: Val Duchesse. Contact: Marianne Amssons (322) 284 2233. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "The impact and effects of the single market" (1115/1215 GMT). Speaker is European Commissioner Monti. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911. BRUSSELS - European Women's Lobby holds press reception for the launch of the Centre on Violence Against Women (1500/1400 GMT). Venue: European Women's Lobby, 22 rue du Meridien. Contact: European Women's Lobby (322) 217 9020. BRUSSELS - European Information Technology Observatory (EITO) holds news conference (1100/1000 GMT). Discussions focus on the latest statistics and forecasts about the European market for information technology hardware and software, including communications technology; current and future technological trends and standards; the future of the Internet; electronic commerce over the Internet. Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: EITO (32) 69 6603 1530. WEDNESDAY, MARCH 5 BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0800 GMT). Provisional agenda includes: - Taxation on energy products. - Fixing of agricultural prices for 1997-98. - Proposal for joint action on the protection of displaced persons. - Proposal on the elimination of customs duties on information technology products and certain alcoholic beverages. - Association countries participation in certain Community programmes. - Action plan on satellite communications in the framework of the information society. - Single document on objective 2 aid for Luxembourg and the Netherlands. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Belgian King Albert visits European Commission and Council of Ministers. Agenda includes: - (1100/1000 GMT) Meets European Commission President Santer; - (1135/1035 GMT) Beginning of the working session; - (1300/1200 GMT) Round table before lunch. - (1445/1345 GMT) Meets Council Secretary General Juergen Trumpf. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP and Central and Eastern European countries hold fourth conference; EP President Jose Maria Gil-Robles holds bilateral discussions with parliament speakers of these countries; holds news conference at 1115/1015 GMT. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) Women's Committee and the European Women's Lobby hold joint news conference on "Give constitutional force to gender equity at European level" (1030/0930 GMT). Venue: International Trade Union House (ITUH), 155 Blvd Emile Jacqmain. Contact: ETUC (322) 224 0411. BRUSSELS - ECOSOC holds hearing on an update and review of the single market (1000/0900 GMT). Venue: ECOSOC. Contact: ECOSOC (322) 546 9207. BRUSSELS - Club de Bruxelles holds conference on "Environment in Europe - The new strategy for waste management - Improving air quality - The new policy on noise pollution" (0915/0815 GMT) (to Friday). Speakers include: MEP Ken Collins. Venue: Management Centre Europe, 118 rue de l'Aqueduc. Contact: Club de Bruxelles (322) 743 1520. Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 3/3 - Thursday-Sunday) THURSDAY, MARCH 6 BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Telecoms Council (1000/0900 GMT). Agenda includes: - Proposal for an EP and Council directive on the application of open network provision (ONP) to voice telephony and on universal service for telecommunications in a competitive environment (replacing EP and Council directive 95/62/EC). - Co-decision procedures with the EP. - Commission report on the Universal Mobile Telecommunications Systems technology. - Application of member state legislation in the telecoms sector. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer meets British Foreign Shadow Minister Robin Cook. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Flynn holds news conference on equal rights between men and women for the international women's day (1200/1100 GMT). BRUSSELS - Conference Board Europe and American Electronics Association Europe hold joint conference on "The information society and electronic commerce". Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: Stephanie Holmgren, AEA Europe (322) 502 6734. LOUVAIN-LA-NEUVE, Belgium (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer addresses European Studies Institute on "Values and references for European construction" (2015/1915 GMT). Venue: Auditoire Socrate, Place Cardinal Mercier. Contact: European Studies Institute (3210) 47 85 45. PARIS - CICERO Foundation holds conference on "Results of the IGC - preparing the Amsterdam treaty". Agenda includes: the issue of flexibility - will Britain block "Core Europe"?; is the Dutch presidency preparing a special strategy?; reforming the Common Foreign and Security Policy - the chances for a Mr CFSP; a breakthrough in the third pillar (justice and home affairs); institutional arrangements - power struggle or compromise?; the IGC seen from Central and Eastern Europe. Contact: CICERO Foundation (33) 1 42 67 9204. WARSAW - CER, UIC and UNIFE hold joint conference on "The pan-European dimension of rail transport" (0900/0800 GMT). Contact: Rita Moosen, CER (322) 525 9079. WELS-UPPER, Austria - Energiesparverband, in cooperation with the European Commission, holds conference on "World energy efficiency day" (0800/0700 GMT). Discussions focus on energy efficiency-the gateway to our future; local and regional strategies for energy efficiency; energy efficiency in industry. Venue: City Hall. Contact: Energiesparverband (43) 732 6584 4380. FRIDAY, MARCH 7 BRUSSELS (MODIFIED ITEM) - U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen meets NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, NATO Military Committee Chairman General Klaus Naumann; attends roundtable of NATO ambassadors. Holds joint news conference with Solana (1645/1545). BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts conference on priority actions for completion of the single market. BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP and Council Conciliation Committee meets to discuss decision on a series of guidelines for trans-European telecoms networks. Commissioner Bangemann attends. BRUSSELS - European disability forum - founding general assembly (0900/0800 GMT) (and Saturday). Speakers include: MEPs Barbara Schmidbauer, Richard Howitt, Bartho Pronk. Venue: Vlaams Europees Conferentie Centrum, 1-3 rue du Marquis. SATURDAY, MARCH 8 LUXEMBOURG - Forex Luxembourg celebrates its 40th anniversary. European Commission President Santer and Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker attend. SUNDAY, MARCH 9 GENEVA (NEW ITEM) - EP Intergroup Tibet, Radical Party, European Tibet Support Group, Tibetan Communities in Europe hold second European demonstration for the freedom of Tibet (1300/1200 GMT) (To March 10). Speakers include: European Commissioner Bonino and MEP James Moorhouse. Venue: In front of the U.N. building. Contact: Geneve 1997 (41) 22 740 4544.
